mainTopic: רבי שמעון's rule on carrying, כבוד הבריות and a corpse in a כרמלית, partial removal of טומאה, and the משנה on removing nails and hair, braiding, and makeup on שבת
overview: This amud opens with the end of רבי שמעון's ruling that one who carries a corpse out to bury it is exempt. רבא adds that רבי שמעון agrees one is liable for carrying a hoe to dig or a ספר תורה to read, because using the object is enough. Next, רב נחמן בר יצחק allows a body to be moved into a כרמלית on שבת, because כבוד הבריות overrides a rabbinic prohibition. Then רב נחמן and רב ששת argue whether plucking one of three white hairs of צרעת counts, and each explains a משנה about half a כזית of a corpse to fit his view. A new משנה follows about removing nails and hair without a tool, braiding, and makeup: רבי אליעזר says liable, and חכמים forbid it only as a שבות. רבי אלעזר limits the dispute: with a tool everyone says liable, and for someone else's nails everyone says exempt. The גמרא sets the measure for hair at two hairs and gives רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's rule for a mostly torn nail, which is the הלכה. Finally, the גמרא asks which מלאכה braiding, eye shadow, and blush fall under, and רבי אבהו begins a corrected explanation that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי שמעון exempts even carrying a corpse for burial
steps.stepSummary: These are the closing words of רבי שמעון's ruling: even someone who carries a dead body out to bury it is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: [רבי שמעון exempts] even one who carries out a dead body to bury it.
steps.whatsHappening: This amud begins in the middle of a sentence. These words finish רבי שמעון's ruling from the previous section, that carrying out a corpse for burial is exempt on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that a מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה does not make a person liable. That is a labor done without wanting the actual purpose the Torah's labor is about. The person carrying the body does not want the body itself in the new place; he only wants it out of his way. So רבי שמעון exempts him from a חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: one who carries out from one domain to another

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new statement. It is the tail end of רבי שמעון's ruling that started on the previous amud.

phrases.english: even regarding one who carries out the corpse
to bury it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the רבי שמעון ruling carried over earlier
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, carrying out a corpse for burial is exempt, because it is a מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה.

steps.title: רבא: רבי שמעון agrees that carrying a hoe to dig or a ספר תורה to read is liable
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that רבי שמעון agrees a person is liable when he carries a hoe in order to dig with it, or a ספר תורה in order to read from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: רבי שמעון agrees that if someone carries out a hoe to dig with it, or a ספר תורה to read from it, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא sets a limit on רבי שמעון's exemption. Carrying an object because you want to use it is a real, liable carrying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the person wants the object itself in the new place, so he can use it there. That is the exact purpose of the labor of carrying. It is therefore a מלאכה שצריכה לגופה, and the person is חייב even according to רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: Rava said:
And Rabbi Shimon agrees
regarding a hoe, to dig with it
and a Torah scroll, to read from it —
that he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets a boundary on the exemption stated in step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Carrying an object in order to use it is liable even according to רבי שמעון.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבא needed to say this. If these cases were exempt too, there would be no liable carrying at all for רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious! If these cases also counted as a labor not needed for its own sake, then how could you ever find a labor that is needed for its own sake according to רבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's statement as too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying a tool to use it is the most basic kind of carrying there is. If even this were called a מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה, רבי שמעון would never hold anyone liable for carrying. So why would רבא bother to teach it?

keyTerms.meaning: a labor done not for its own purpose
how could you find such a case?

phrases.english: It is obvious,
for if this too
is a labor not needed for its own sake,
then a labor that is needed for its own sake,
according to Rabbi Shimon, how would you find it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for רבא's statement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without these cases, רבי שמעון would have no liable carrying at all. So the statement teaches nothing new.

steps.title: רבא's point: no need for a benefit to the object too
steps.stepSummary: One might have thought רבי שמעון requires the carrying to serve both the person and the object itself. רבא teaches that serving the person is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that a person is only liable when the carrying is both for his own use and for the object's sake. For example, carrying a hoe to fix its blade and also to dig, or a ספר תורה to correct it and also to read from it. So רבא teaches us that this is not needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבא's statement does add something new. Using the object is enough for liability, even if nothing is done to the object itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mistaken idea was that liability requires both לגופו (for the person) and לגופה (for the object). רבא clarifies that a purpose for the person alone, digging or reading, already counts as צריכה לגופה.

keyTerms.meaning: for his (the person's) sake and for its (the object's) sake

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, carrying an object in order to use it is enough for liability according to רבי שמעון. The carrying does not also need to benefit the object.

phrases.english: You might have said
that he is not liable unless it is for his sake and for its sake,

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן מָר לַעֲשׂוֹת לוֹ טַס וְלַחְפּוֹר,
phrases.english: for example, a hoe, to fix its blade and to dig,
or a Torah scroll, to correct it and to read from it,
so he teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a possible mistaken assumption that the statement rules out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Liability requires a purpose both for the person and for the object
steps.terutzMaskana: A purpose for the person alone, such as digging or reading, is enough for liability

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק permits moving a body into a כרמלית
steps.stepSummary: A body was lying in דרוקרת, and רב נחמן בר יצחק allowed it to be carried into a כרמלית on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a dead body in דרוקרת. רב נחמן בר יצחק permitted carrying it out to a כרמלית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story of a practical ruling. This sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כרמלית is an area that is only rabbinically treated like a public domain. The question will be what basis allowed this ruling, since carrying into a כרמלית is still forbidden מדרבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: an in-between domain, forbidden only by rabbinic law

phrases.english: There was a certain corpse in Derokeret;
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak permitted
to carry it out to a karmelit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A practical story connected to carrying a corpse
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Moving the body into a כרמלית on שבת was permitted.

steps.title: Even רבי שמעון leaves a rabbinic prohibition
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, brother of מר בריה דרבנא, challenges the ruling. Even if it follows רבי שמעון, there is still a rabbinic prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן, the brother of מר son of רבנא, said to רב נחמן בר יצחק: Whose opinion did you follow, רבי שמעון's? Granted that רבי שמעון exempts a person from bringing a חטאת, but there is still a rabbinic prohibition!
steps.whatsHappening: The ruling is challenged. רבי שמעון's exemption only removes the Torah-level penalty, not the איסור דרבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פטור in רבי שמעון's view means no חטאת. It does not mean the act is allowed. So relying on רבי שמעון does not seem to be enough to permit it.
steps.confusionAlert: Saying פטור about רבי שמעון here does not mean 'permitted.' It only means there is no חטאת.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said to him,
the brother of Mar son of Rabbana,
to Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak:
According to whom? According to Rabbi Shimon?

phrases.aramaic: אֵימַר דְּפָטַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מֵחִיּוּב חַטָּאת,
phrases.english: Granted that Rabbi Shimon exempts from the obligation of a sin-offering,
but a rabbinic prohibition at least remains!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling in step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן בר יצחק's permission to move the body
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון's exemption only removes the חטאת. A rabbinic prohibition remains, so the act should still be forbidden.

steps.title: A כרמלית is only rabbinic, and כבוד הבריות overrides it
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that he only permitted a כרמלית, which is rabbinic. כבוד הבריות overrides rabbinic prohibitions, so the ruling holds even according to רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: By God! Did you even look into it? It is permitted even according to רבי יהודה. Did I say to carry it into a רשות הרבים? I said a כרמלית. Great is human dignity, for it pushes aside a 'לא תעשה' of the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains the real basis for his ruling. It does not depend on רבי שמעון at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying into a כרמלית is only an איסור דרבנן. The principle of כבוד הבריות overrides rabbinic prohibitions. The 'לא תעשה' mentioned refers to 'לא תסור,' the Torah's command to obey the Sages, which is the source of all rabbinic laws. So the ruling works even for רבי יהודה, who holds that a מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה is liable.
steps.whatToRemember: כבוד הבריות overrides rabbinic prohibitions, such as carrying a body into a כרמלית on שבת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a key source for the halachic principle that human dignity can set aside a rabbinic law.

phrases.english: He said to him:
By God! Have you entered into the matter?
Even according to Rabbi Yehuda it is permitted,
for did I say to the public domain?
I said to a karmelit,
great is human dignity,
for it overrides a prohibition of the Torah.
phrases.notes: Refers to לא תסור, the Torah basis of rabbinic law

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframes the basis of the ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling relied on רבי שמעון's exemption
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling relies on כבוד הבריות overriding the rabbinic prohibition of a כרמלית, so it holds even for רבי יהודה

steps.title: משנה: plucking signs of צרעת טומאה is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: A משנה elsewhere teaches that one who plucks out signs of טומאה or burns away the healthy skin violates a לא תעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there in a משנה: One who plucks out signs of טומאה, or burns away the healthy skin, violates a negative commandment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source about צרעת. It is setting up an אמוראים dispute based on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Removing the signs of צרעת in order to become טהור is forbidden. The new topic connects to the theme of whether an action that does not fully achieve its goal is considered meaningful.

keyTerms.meaning: signs of impurity (white hairs of צרעת)
healthy flesh within the צרעת patch

phrases.english: We learned there:
One who plucks out signs of impurity
and one who burns the healthy flesh
violates a negative commandment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Removing signs of צרעת violates a לא תעשה.

steps.title: Plucking one of two hairs versus one of three
steps.stepSummary: Plucking one of two white hairs is liable. For one of three, רב נחמן says liable and רב ששת says exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said: If someone plucks one of two hairs, he is liable. If he plucks one of three, רב נחמן says he is liable and רב ששת says he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents a dispute between אמוראים about an action that does not fully remove the טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two white hairs are the minimum sign of טומאה. Plucking one of two removes the טומאה, so he is liable. Plucking one of three still leaves two hairs, so the person is still טמא. That is why there is a dispute.

phrases.english: It was stated:
One of two — he is liable;
one of three —
Rav Nachman said he is liable,
Rav Sheshet said he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a dispute on the משנה in step 8
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One of two is liable. One of three is disputed between רב נחמן and רב ששת.

steps.title: The reasoning of each side
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן: his action was effective, because one more pluck would remove the טומאה. רב ששת: for now the טומאה is still fully there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said liable: his action accomplished something, because if one more hair is removed, the טומאה is gone. רב ששת said exempt: for now, at least, the טומאה is still there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind each opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן looks at progress: the person moved closer to טהרה. רב ששת looks at the present result: nothing has changed yet, since the person is still טמא.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said he is liable —
his actions were effective,
for if one more is removed
the impurity goes away.
Rav Sheshet said he is exempt —
now, at any rate, the impurity is still there.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר חַיָּיב — אַהְנִי מַעֲשָׂיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the dispute in step 9
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן counts partial progress toward removing טומאה. רב ששת requires an actual change in status.

steps.title: רב ששת's source: a contradiction about half an olive-bulk
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת brings a משנה implying that carrying half a כזית of a corpse is exempt, and a ברייתא saying it is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: How do I know this? We learned in a משנה: Likewise, a כזית of a corpse or a כזית of a נבלה, he is liable. This implies that half a כזית is exempt. But a ברייתא teaches: half a כזית, he is liable!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת begins his proof by pointing out a contradiction between two sources. He is setting up a resolution that will support his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה implies that half a כזית of a corpse is פטור, while the ברייתא says it is חייב. The way this contradiction gets resolved will become רב ששת's proof.

keyTerms.meaning: from where do I say it?

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
From where do I say it?
As we learned: And likewise an olive-bulk of a corpse
and an olive-bulk of a carcass — he is liable;
this implies half an olive-bulk — exempt;
but it was taught: 'Half an olive-bulk — liable'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins רב ששת's proof for his view in steps 9 and 10
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's view that a partial action that leaves the טומאה intact is exempt
steps.raayaSupportSource: A contradiction between the משנה (half a כזית exempt) and the ברייתא (half a כזית liable)

steps.title: Resolving the contradiction supports רב ששת
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא (liable) is when half a כזית was taken from a whole כזית. The משנה (exempt) is when it was taken from one and a half כזיתים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it not that the ברייתא saying 'liable' is when he took out half a כזית from a single כזית, and the משנה saying 'exempt' is when he took out half a כזית from a כזית and a half?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת resolves the contradiction in a way that matches his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking half from exactly one כזית ruins the source of טומאה, so he is liable. Taking half from one and a half leaves a full כזית, so the טומאה stays and he is exempt. This exactly matches 'one of three hairs' being exempt.

phrases.english: Is it not that
this which was taught 'liable' —
is where he took out half an olive-bulk from an olive-bulk,
and this which we learned 'exempt' —
is where he took out half an olive-bulk from an olive-bulk and a half.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in step 11
steps.raayaSupportSource: The resolution of the משנה and ברייתא based on whether a full כזית remains

steps.title: רב נחמן: the exempt case is a large corpse
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן holds both cases are liable. The משנה's exemption refers to taking half a כזית from a large corpse.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן? Both this case and that case are liable. The משנה that says 'exempt' is talking about someone who took out half a כזית from a large corpse.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן deflects רב ששת's proof by explaining the משנה differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking half a כזית from a full corpse brings it no closer to טהרה at all, so even רב נחמן agrees it is exempt. In the one-and-a-half case, there is real progress toward removing the טומאה, so רב נחמן says liable. The sources do not force רב ששת's view.
steps.whatToRemember: רב ששת and רב נחמן disagree about whether partial progress toward removing טומאה counts. Each explains the משנה about half a כזית in a way that fits his own view.

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman?
Both this and that are liable,
and that which we learned 'exempt'
is where he took out half an olive-bulk from a large corpse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 12
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב ששת's reading of the משנה, not the משנה itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה's exempt case can be explained as a large corpse, where no progress toward טהרה happens, so the sources do not prove רב ששת's view

steps.title: New משנה: removing nails and hair, braiding, and makeup
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists several actions: removing nails with nails or teeth, pulling out hair, mustache or beard, braiding, and applying makeup. רבי אליעזר holds one liable, and חכמים forbid them only as a שבות.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone removes his fingernails using his other nails or his teeth. The same goes for his hair, his mustache, and his beard. The same goes for a woman who braids her hair, one who puts on eye makeup, and one who puts on blush. רבי אליעזר says all of these are liable. חכמים say they are forbidden only because of a rabbinic decree (שבות).
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens a new topic: grooming and beautifying actions done on שבת without the normal tool.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The nail and hair cases are done in an unusual way, with fingers or teeth instead of scissors. Braiding and makeup are grooming acts that do not obviously match any מלאכה; step 34 asks which מלאכה they would be. רבי אליעזר says all of these count as a Torah מלאכה, so one is liable. חכמים say none of them is a real מלאכה, and they are only forbidden by the Rabbis.

keyTerms.meaning: One with the other (nail against nail, without a tool)
A woman who applies eye makeup (כחול)
A woman who applies blush or rouge
A rabbinic prohibition on שבת (not a Torah מלאכה)

steps.confusionAlert: חכמים do not permit these actions. They are still forbidden. The argument is only whether this is a Torah violation (liable for a קרבן) or a rabbinic one (שבות).

phrases.english: Mishnah:
One who removes his fingernails one with the other,
or with his teeth,
and likewise his hair, and likewise his mustache,
and likewise his beard,
and likewise a woman who braids,
and likewise one who applies eye makeup, and likewise one who applies blush —
Rabbi Eliezer holds liable,
and the Sages forbid it because of a rabbinic decree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic, separate from the previous discussion of white hairs and טומאת מת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Grooming done without a tool: רבי אליעזר says liable by Torah law, and חכמים say forbidden only as a שבות.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: the dispute is only by hand; with a tool everyone says liable
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר limits the dispute to removing nails by hand. With a tool, even חכמים agree one is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי אלעזר said: The argument is only when he removes the nails by hand. But if he uses a tool, everyone agrees he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with רבי אלעזר, who explains exactly where רבי אליעזר and חכמים disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים exempt only because the act was done in an unusual way, by hand. With a tool such as scissors, the act is done the normal way, so it is a full Torah מלאכה for everyone.

phrases.english: Gemara: Rabbi Elazar said:
The dispute is by hand,
but with a utensil — he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the scope of the dispute in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Removing nails with a tool on שבת makes one liable according to everyone.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious from the words 'one with the other'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי אלעזר needs to say this. The משנה already says 'זו בזו', which shows it is talking about removal by hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious! We learned in the משנה 'one with the other'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר: his statement seems to add nothing to what the משנה already says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה describes the case as nail against nail. So it is clear that the dispute is about doing it by hand. Why would רבי אלעזר need to tell us this?

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious (a challenge that a statement is unnecessary)

phrases.english: It is obvious,
we learned 'one with the other'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether רבי אלעזר's statement is needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's statement that the dispute is only by hand
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wording 'זו בזו' already limits the case to removal by hand, so the statement seems unnecessary.

steps.title: We might have thought חכמים exempt even with a tool
steps.stepSummary: Without רבי אלעזר, we might have thought חכמים exempt even with a tool. We might have read 'זו בזו' as showing how far רבי אליעזר goes. רבי אלעזר teaches that this is not so.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: חכמים exempt even with a tool, and the משנה said 'one with the other' only to show how far רבי אליעזר's view goes. So רבי אלעזר teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the wording of the משנה could have been misread. רבי אלעזר's statement prevents that mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'זו בזו' could mean that the dispute covers every case, and the משנה mentions removal by hand only because it is the strongest case for רבי אליעזר: even then he says liable. רבי אלעזר tells us the opposite. The dispute really is limited to removal by hand, and with a tool even חכמים say liable.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces the mistaken assumption)
To show you the strength (how far a view goes)
He teaches us (that the assumption is wrong)

phrases.english: Lest you say:
the Rabbis exempt even with a utensil,
and that which it teaches 'one with the other' —
is to inform you of the strength of Rabbi Eliezer's view,
so he teaches us.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: רַבָּנַן בִּכְלִי נָמֵי פָּטְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the wording of the משנה was ambiguous
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'זו בזו' only shows how far רבי אליעזר goes, and חכמים exempt even with a tool.
steps.terutzMaskana: With a tool, everyone agrees one is liable. The dispute is only about removal by hand.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: the dispute is only for oneself; for another everyone says exempt
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר gives a second limit. The dispute is only about cutting one's own nails. Cutting someone else's nails by hand is exempt according to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said: The argument is only when he does it to himself. But if he does it to his friend, everyone agrees he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר adds a second limit to the dispute in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Removing your own nails with your other nails is something a person can do somewhat effectively. Removing a friend's nails this way is even more unusual. So even רבי אליעזר agrees there is no Torah liability.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
The dispute is for himself,
but for his friend — all agree he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second statement of רבי אלעזר, again limiting the dispute. Here the limit runs toward exemption.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Removing another person's nails by hand is exempt according to everyone.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious from the words 'his fingernails'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why this is needed. The משנה says 'צפרניו', his own nails.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious! We learned 'his fingernails'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second statement the same way it challenged the first: the משנה already says this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה specifically says 'his nails'. So it is already clear that the dispute is about one's own nails. רבי אלעזר seems to add nothing.

phrases.english: It is obvious, we learned 'his fingernails'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same 'obvious' challenge, now on the second statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's statement that the dispute is only for oneself
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'צפרניו' (his nails) already limits the case to one's own nails.

steps.title: We might have thought רבי אליעזר obligates even for another
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought רבי אליעזר obligates even for someone else's nails. We might have read 'his nails' as showing how far חכמים go. רבי אלעזר teaches that this is not so.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: רבי אליעזר holds one liable even for a friend's nails, and the משנה said 'his nails' only to show how far חכמים go. So רבי אלעזר teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'his nails' could have been misread. רבי אלעזר's statement makes the real meaning clear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This mirrors the first answer, but in reverse. 'His nails' might have been the strongest case for חכמים: they exempt even one's own nails, and of course a friend's. Then רבי אליעזר would hold liable in both cases. רבי אלעזר teaches that for a friend's nails, even רבי אליעזר exempts.

keyTerms.meaning: The strength of the Rabbis' view

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר places the dispute between two edges. With a tool, everyone says liable. Doing it to someone else, everyone says exempt. רבי אליעזר and חכמים argue only about removing your own nails by hand.

phrases.english: Lest you say
Rabbi Eliezer holds liable for his friend too,
and that which it teaches 'his fingernails'
is to inform you of the strength of the Rabbis' view,
so he teaches us.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְתֵימָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לַחֲבֵירוֹ נָמֵי מְחַיַּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge, parallel to step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the wording of the משנה was ambiguous
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'צפרניו' only shows how far חכמים go, and רבי אליעזר holds liable even for a friend's nails.
steps.terutzMaskana: For a friend's nails, everyone agrees one is exempt.

steps.title: A ברייתא: removing a scissors-full of hair makes one liable
steps.stepSummary: Turning to the משנה's case of hair, a ברייתא teaches that removing 'מלא פי הזוג' (enough to fill the scissors' opening) makes one liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Regarding 'and likewise his hair': It was taught: One who removes enough hair to fill the opening of the scissors is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next phrase of the משנה, about hair, and brings a ברייתא that sets the minimum amount for liability.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every Torah מלאכה needs a minimum amount before one is liable. For removing hair, the measure is 'a scissors-full'. That leaves open how many hairs this is, which the גמרא asks next.

keyTerms.meaning: Enough to fill the opening of the scissors

phrases.english: 'And likewise his hair' etc.
It was taught:
One who removes the full opening of the scissors — is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the nail discussion to the hair clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Removing a scissors-full of hair on שבת makes one liable.

steps.title: How much is a scissors-full?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how many hairs make up 'מלא פי הזוג'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much is a scissors-full?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a clear number behind the vague phrase 'a scissors-full'. This sets up רב יהודה's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'A scissors-full' is not precise. To apply the law, we need an exact number of hairs.

phrases.english: And how much is the full opening of the scissors?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the exact meaning of the ברייתא's measure.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The number of hairs that equals 'מלא פי הזוג'.

steps.title: רב יהודה: two hairs
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers that a scissors-full is two hairs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: Two.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives the number: removing two hairs makes one liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Scissors can grip and cut as few as two hairs. So two hairs is the smallest amount that counts as a real act of shearing.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: Two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question.

steps.title: Challenge: the ברייתא lists 'two' separately for baldness
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues 'and for קרחה, two'. The word 'and' suggests 'two' is a different measure from 'a scissors-full', which would contradict רב יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: 'And for baldness, two'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה from the same ברייתא, which seems to set 'two' as a separate measure for קרחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first says 'a scissors-full' for שבת and then 'and for קרחה (the mourning prohibition), two'. Using a different phrase suggests a different amount. So 'a scissors-full' would not mean two hairs.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught (introduces a challenge from a ברייתא)
Making a bald spot in mourning, forbidden by the Torah

phrases.english: But was it not taught:
'And for baldness, two'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יהודה's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's claim that 'מלא פי הזוג' is two hairs
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא gives 'two' as a separate measure for קרחה, which implies 'a scissors-full' is a different amount.

steps.title: Read it as 'and likewise for baldness, two'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא as 'וכן לקרחה שתים': the measure for קרחה is the same two hairs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: 'And likewise for baldness, two.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by rereading the ברייתא so that it agrees with רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is not giving a new, different measure. It is saying that קרחה has the same measure as שבת, which is two hairs. So רב יהודה stands.
steps.whatToRemember: Removing two hairs on שבת makes one liable, since that is 'a scissors-full'. The same two-hair measure applies to the Torah prohibition of קרחה.

phrases.english: Say:
'And likewise for baldness, two.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge to רב יהודה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'And for קרחה, two' is a separate measure, different from 'a scissors-full'.
steps.terutzMaskana: Read it as 'and likewise': both שבת and קרחה use the same two-hair measure.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports that a scissors-full is two hairs
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא is quoted that says outright that a scissors-full is two hairs, backing up רב יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This was also taught in a ברייתא: One who removes a scissors-full of hair on שבת is liable. And how much is a scissors-full? Two hairs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what רב יהודה said: a scissors-full means two hairs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, רב יהודה's measure of two hairs came from his own reading. Now a ברייתא states it openly. The phrase תניא נמי הכי means 'a ברייתא also teaches this,' and it always signals support.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a ברייתא that supports the last statement)

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:

phrases.aramaic: הַנּוֹטֵל מְלֹא פִי הַזּוּג בְּשַׁבָּת — חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: One who removes enough hair to fill the scissors' opening on Shabbat is liable.
And how much is a scissors-full? Two hairs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms רב יהודה's measure after the challenge in step 24 was answered in step 25.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's ruling that a scissors-full is two hairs
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that defines a scissors-full as two hairs

steps.title: רבי אליעזר says even one hair, and the חכמים agree when picking white hairs
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר holds that even one hair makes one liable. The חכמים agree with him when someone picks white hairs out from black ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: even one hair. And the חכמים agree with רבי אליעזר about someone who picks white hairs out from among black ones: even for one hair, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא continues. It gives רבי אליעזר's stricter view of one hair and one case where the חכמים agree with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים require two hairs because one hair normally does not matter to a person. But someone picking out white hairs cares about every single one, so his action shows that one hair is important to him. That is why even the חכמים hold him liable for one hair here.

keyTerms.meaning: White hairs from among black ones

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: one hair,
and the Sages agree with Rabbi Eliezer
about one who picks white hairs from among black ones,
that even for one hair he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, adding the dissent of רבי אליעזר and one case where the חכמים agree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר holds one hair makes one liable. The חכמים agree when someone picks white hairs from black, because there every hair matters to him.

steps.title: Picking white hairs is forbidden for men even on a weekday
steps.stepSummary: Picking out white hairs is forbidden even on a weekday, because of the פסוק 'a man shall not wear a woman's garment.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And this thing is forbidden even on a weekday, because it says: 'A man shall not wear a woman's garment.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a weekday rule. Picking out white hairs is forbidden for a man even when it is not שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picking out white hairs is a way of beautifying oneself that women usually do. The פסוק of לא ילבש גבר שמלת אשה is understood to forbid men from doing women's beautifying acts. So this ban has nothing to do with שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: A man shall not wear a woman's garment (דברים 22:5)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a שבת law. It is a separate, all-week ban based on the פסוק, mentioned here only because the case came up.

phrases.english: And this thing is forbidden even on a weekday,
because it is said:
"A man shall not wear a woman's garment."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a weekday ban about the same act described in step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Picking white hairs from black is forbidden for men even on weekdays, based on לא ילבש גבר שמלת אשה.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר on a mostly torn nail or loose skin
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר teaches that a nail or bits of skin that are mostly torn off may be removed by hand, but removing them with a tool makes one liable for a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: a nail that is mostly torn off, and bits of skin that are mostly torn off: by hand it is permitted, with a tool one is liable for a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about nails, which the משנה also mentions. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר gives the rule for a nail or skin that is already mostly detached.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two things matter here: how much is already torn off, and whether a hand or a tool is used. As written, the ברייתא says a hand is completely permitted while a tool brings a חטאת. That big gap is what the גמרא will question next.

keyTerms.meaning: Loose bits of skin around the nail
Liable to bring a sin-offering (a Torah-level violation)

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
a fingernail that is mostly detached,
and skin shreds that are mostly detached,
removing them by hand is permitted;
with a utensil, one is liable to bring a sin-offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from hair to the משנה's case of nails.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mostly detached nail or skin: by hand it is permitted, with a tool one is liable for a חטאת (as the text first reads).

steps.title: How can a tool bring a חטאת while the hand is fully permitted?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the gap is too big. If a tool makes it a Torah violation, how can doing it by hand be fully permitted?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there anything where with a tool one is liable for a חטאת, and by hand it is permitted from the start?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges how the ברייתא reads. It is hard to believe the same act jumps from fully permitted to a Torah violation just by switching from hand to tool.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, doing a מלאכה by hand is the unusual way. That makes it פטור אבל אסור, meaning not a Torah violation but still rabbinically forbidden. It should not be completely permitted. So the ברייתא skips a middle level, and that seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Is there anything such that...? (a challenging question)
From the start, permitted up front

phrases.aramaic: מִי אִיכָּא מִידֵּי דְּבִכְלִי חַיָּיב חַטָּאת,
phrases.english: Is there anything where with a utensil one is liable to a sin-offering,
and by hand it is permitted from the outset?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the plain reading of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The plain reading of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's ruling in step 29
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule as read jumps from fully permitted (hand) straight to a Torah violation (tool), skipping the expected middle level of פטור אבל אסור.

steps.title: Re-explaining the ברייתא as two separate cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר was describing two cases, mostly detached and not mostly detached, and each one moves down by just one level.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: If it is mostly detached, by hand it is permitted, and with a tool it is פטור but forbidden. If it is not mostly detached, by hand it is פטור but forbidden, and with a tool one is liable for a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the ברייתא as two cases, each with its own hand rule and tool rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are now four outcomes on a ladder: permitted, then פטור אבל אסור, then חייב חטאת. Being mostly detached lowers the seriousness by one step, and so does using a hand instead of a tool. That way nothing ever jumps two levels at once.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means (a re-reading)
Not a Torah violation, but still rabbinically forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: Mostly detached: hand is permitted, tool is פטור אבל אסור. Not mostly detached: hand is פטור אבל אסור, tool is חייב חטאת.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
if mostly detached, by hand it is permitted,
with a utensil, exempt but forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא פֵּירְשׁוּ רוּבָּן, בַּיָּד — פָּטוּר אֲבָל אָסוּר,
phrases.english: If not mostly detached, by hand it is exempt but forbidden,
with a utensil, liable to a sin-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 30 by re-reading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading: the ברייתא actually describes two separate cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא described one case, with the hand fully permitted and the tool bringing a חטאת.
steps.terutzMaskana: There are two cases (mostly detached or not), and in each the change from tool to hand lowers the seriousness by exactly one level.

steps.title: רב יהודה rules like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: The הלכה is like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives the practical ruling: we follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's rule about nails and skin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This makes the re-explained ברייתא the practical law. So a mostly detached nail may actually be removed by hand on שבת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical source for being allowed to remove a mostly torn nail by hand on שבת.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling on the re-explained ברייתא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: a mostly detached nail or skin may be removed by hand.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's condition: only when it points upward and hurts
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן adds that the permission applies only when the torn piece is lifted upward toward the nail and is causing pain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: This is only when they are torn upward and they are causing him pain.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן narrows the permission. You may remove the piece by hand only if it is lifted upward and bothering you.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being mostly detached is not enough by itself. The piece must also stick up and cause pain. When both are true, the rabbis allowed removing it by hand to spare the person discomfort.

keyTerms.meaning: And this applies only when... (adds a condition)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
and that is only when they are detached facing upward
and they cause him pain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the permission that רב יהודה ruled on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Removing a mostly detached piece by hand is permitted only when it points upward and causes pain.

steps.title: Which מלאכה is violated by braiding, eye shadow, and blush?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's next case and asks which מלאכה makes a woman liable for braiding hair, applying eye shadow, or applying blush.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And so too a woman who braids...' For which מלאכה is a woman who braids, puts on eye shadow, or puts on blush held liable?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes the next case. Then it asks which of the 39 מלאכות these three beauty acts fall under.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי אליעזר holds that these acts bring a Torah-level liability. But being liable requires a specific מלאכה, and none of these acts obviously matches one. So the גמרא asks for the source of the liability.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who braids her hair
A woman who applies כחול (eye shadow)

phrases.english: The mishna said: "And so too one who braids," etc.
A woman who braids, applies eye shadow, or applies blush:
for what prohibited labor is she liable?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next phrase of the משנה, a new topic.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which of the 39 מלאכות makes one liable for braiding, eye shadow, and blush according to רבי אליעזר

steps.title: Braiding is like weaving, eye shadow like writing, blush like spinning
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, quoted by רבי אבין, matches each act to a מלאכה: braiding to weaving, eye shadow to writing, blush to spinning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין said in the name of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא: A woman who braids is liable for weaving, one who applies eye shadow for writing, and one who applies blush for spinning.
steps.whatsHappening: An answer is given that pairs each beauty act with a מלאכה that looks similar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Braiding twists strands together, much like weaving. Painting a line on the eye looks like writing. Blush was made by rolling a doughy string and running it over the face, which resembles spinning. Each match is based on how the act looks.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Avin said that Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said:
one who braids is liable for weaving,
one who applies eye shadow, for writing,
one who applies blush, for spinning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 34.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Braiding is weaving, eye shadow is writing, and blush is spinning.

steps.title: The רבנן object: that is not the normal way to do these מלאכות
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן tell רבי אבהו that braiding, eye shadow, and blush are not the normal way of weaving, writing, or spinning.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן said before רבי אבהו: Is that the normal way of weaving? Is that the normal way of writing? Is that the normal way of spinning?!
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן challenge the answer of step 35. Nobody weaves, writes, or spins this way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Torah liability on שבת requires doing a מלאכה in its normal way. Doing it in an unusual way, called כלאחר יד, is exempt, and even רבי אליעזר would agree. So these comparisons cannot explain why רבי אליעזר holds a person liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it really the normal way...?

phrases.english: The Rabbis said before Rabbi Abbahu:
Is that the typical manner of weaving?
Is that the typical manner of writing?
Is that the typical manner of spinning?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 35.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparisons of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא in step 35
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A מלאכה done in an unusual way does not bring Torah liability, and these beauty acts are not the normal way to weave, write, or spin.

steps.title: רבי אבהו begins a corrected explanation from רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו rejects the earlier report and begins to give the explanation he heard directly from רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי אבהו said: It was explained to me personally by רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא...
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. רבי אבהו is about to give a different explanation that he heard firsthand, and the explanation itself continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא means the earlier version (weaving, writing, spinning) is being dropped. רבי אבהו says he heard the real explanation from רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא himself, so he has a more reliable account of what he meant.

keyTerms.meaning: It was explained to me personally

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Abbahu said:
It was explained to me personally
by Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, himself,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the קשיא of step 36 by offering a corrected report of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's view (continued on the next amud).
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replacing the earlier report with a firsthand, corrected one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא compared the acts to weaving, writing, and spinning.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אבהו heard a different explanation directly from him, which will be given on the next amud.
